newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica postpones amnesty hearing in Hani killing.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica postpones amnesty hearing in Hani killing.

text.p: An amnesty hearing for the killers of popular black anti-apartheid leader Chris Hani was postponed on Monday until August 11, at his widow's request.

White right-wingers Clive Derby-Lewis and Polish immigrant Janusz Walus are serving life terms for Hani's assassination on April 10, 1993. They were initially sentenced to death but this was commuted to life imprisonment.

Their request for amnesty was due to be heard by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission this week, but lawyers for Hani's widow Limpho said she had prior commitments in the United States and they needed more time to review documents before the amnesty panel.

About 300 supporters of the Communist Party chanted outside the Benoni City Hall east of Johannesburg where the hearing was being held, protesting that Derby-Lewis and Walus did not qualify for amnesty.
A handful of conservative whites sat quietly inside the building, some women knitting and surrounded by picnic hampers with sandwiches and flasks of coffee.
The truth commission was set up in 1995 to heal the wounds of South Africa's apartheid past by investigating human rights abuses on both sides of the racial divide.
